::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Ignore newline in LaTeX variable](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/17867/ignore-newline-in-latex-variable), asked by [jesper](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/3926/jesper) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-05-10; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I have some string in variable `\somevar`, eg. `foo\\bar`. How can I force LaTeX to ignore newline in `\somevar`. When I write content of the variable there should be
> <pre>
> foo bar
> </pre>
> and not
> <pre>
> foo
> bar
> </pre>
:::

Within the group that you are expanding the macro you can do 

```latex
\let\\=\relax
```

This will temporarily neuter the effect of `\\`.
